 Jio Platforms Listing Today: Rs 30,213 crore IPO eyes strong debut on Dalal Street
 SECTIONS Jio Platforms Listing Today: Rs 30,213 crore IPO eyes strong debut on Dalal Street By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 28, 2026, 07:14:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis In a landmark event, Jio Platforms' shares are set to launch in the stock market today after a historic IPO. The exceptional investor demand is underscored by a strong grey market premium, signaling optimistic initial pricing. Market analysts foresee that Jio's vast subscriber network and future expansion capabilities will drive further interest.

 Agencies Jio shares are commanding a grey market premium of around Rs 246-247 over the IPO price of Rs 1,119, indicating a possible listing price of Rs 1,365-1,366.
 Shares of Jio Platforms , the telecom and digital services arm of Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries , are set to make their stock market debut today, following India's biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO). Ahead of the listing, the grey market premium (GMP) of around 22% indicates a strong start for the Rs 30,213 crore issue, which attracted record investor demand.
 Jio shares are commanding a grey market premium of around Rs 246-247 over the IPO price of Rs 1,119, indicating a possible listing price of Rs 1,365-1,366. This translates into potential listing gains of around Rs 2,950 for investors allotted one lot of 12 shares.
The unofficial premium suggests strong buying interest ahead of the debut, although actual listing gains will depend on demand during the opening session. Grey market premiums are unofficial and can fluctuate sharply before trading begins.
Jio's public issue, which opened on October 21 and closed on October 23, was subscribed 22.19 times, with qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) leading the demand. The QIB portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while non-institutional investors bid for 14 times their allotted shares. The retail category was subscribed 2.72 times.
 Also Read: Jio’s big-bang listing may give it stock market’s No.2 crown after Reliance Industries 
 Live Events
 The record subscription and the company's Rs 10.3 lakh crore IPO valuation have made Jio's listing one of the most closely watched market events of the year.
 What analysts expect from Jio's listing
Analysts expect Jio's market leadership, subscriber base and expanding digital businesses to support investor interest beyond its debut.
 Uday Patil, Executive Director at PL Capital, described the listing as a milestone for India's capital markets, citing the company's established telecom operations and opportunities in broadband, cloud computing and artificial intelligence.
"Jio has more than 500 million subscribers and a large telecom network, alongside broadband, enterprise technology, cloud and AI opportunities," Patil said. He believes higher average revenue per user (ARPU), home broadband adoption, enterprise services and monetisation of digital platforms could support the company's future growth.
"Execution will determine how much value these opportunities create," Patil said, adding that Jio offers a long-term investment opportunity.
Motilal Oswal sees room for long-term growth, citing its leadership in India's telecom market, earnings growth and opportunities in emerging digital services. "Jio offers a combination of market leadership, healthy earnings growth and future opportunities in broadband, enterprise technology and AI," the broker said.
It identified ARPU growth, future tariff increases and digital services monetisation as important factors to monitor.
 Record IPO demand puts Jio in the spotlight
Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213 crore IPO surpassed Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore offering to become the largest public issue in India's capital market history. The issue was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening, reflecting strong early participation from institutional and retail investors.
The public book attracted bids worth more than Rs 4.9 lakh crore, while the anchor allocation drew substantial interest from leading domestic and international investors. The IPO attracted more than 1.38 crore applications, according to Investoyard data, setting a new reported record for investor applications.
Jio raised Rs 8,110 crore through its anchor allocation ahead of the public issue, with institutional investors including BlackRock, Fidelity and Life Insurance Corporation of India participating. At the upper end of its price band of Rs 1,065-1,119, Jio Platforms is valued at Rs 10.3 lakh crore, placing it among India's most valuable companies.
The offering comprised 27 crore fresh equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. Existing shareholders, including Reliance Industries and strategic investors, did not sell shares through the IPO.
The company intends to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings at Reliance Jio Infocomm, while the remaining funds will be used for general corporate purposes.
 What investors will watch after listing
Jio enters the market with a subscriber base of more than 53 crore and a nationwide 5G network. Its future earnings growth will depend on tariff revisions, rising data consumption, home broadband expansion and revenue from enterprise technology services.
For FY26, the company reported revenue from operations of Rs 1.47 lakh crore and profit after tax of Rs 30,049 crore. Its EBITDA margin stood at 51.91%.
At a listing premium of 22%, Jio's implied market cap could reach nearly Rs 12.6 lakh crore, giving it a place among India's most valuable listed companies from its first trading session.
The debut will also be closely tracked for its potential impact on Reliance Industries , which will remain Jio Platforms' majority shareholder after the offering.
